sentences.text: Compagopiscis croucheri is a monotypic genus, meaning it contains only one known species. It holds the distinction of being one of the earliest vertebrates known to possess teeth.
The genus was formally described by Gardiner and Miles in 1994.
Analysis of its bite force suggests Compagopiscis was a generalist predator capable of consuming a diverse diet.
The abundance of fossils suggests that Compagopiscis may have exhibited schooling behavior.

Taxonomically, Compagopiscis belongs to the class Placodermi. Phylogenetic analysis places it within the clade Coccosteomorphi, part of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea and the group Eubrachythoraci. Its immediate parent group is the family Panxiosteidae.
This animal lived in Western Australia during the Upper Devonian, specifically the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
